cluster_name: Federal judge rejects Trump's bid to void hush money conviction
tldr: The headline layer narrows the August 28 judicial triple-bill to a single dominant frame: eight of ten live outlets lead with defeat verbs — 'loses,' 'rejects,' 'denies,' 'blocks' — applied to the hush money case, while body text sustains broader presidential immunity analysis. Only Reuters and The Hindu Intl introduce the pro-Palestinian deportation angle at headline level, and only Straits Times surfaces the birthright citizenship track, so most RSS readers encounter a single-story day rather than the three-front judicial story that body text reveals. Reason alone shifts from outcome to procedural cause ('came too late'), the only headline to make the legal mechanism legible without clicking. China's Xinhua is editorially absent — its sole entry is a stale 2017 travel ban headline — widening the gap between China's stated cluster participation and its actual headline presence.
event_summary: On August 28, 2026, judge Hellerstein denied Trump's bid to transfer his hush money conviction to federal court a third time; a California judge struck down deportation of pro-Palestinian student activists; a Maryland judge declined to block Trump's revised birthright citizenship order.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to frame the ruling as a procedural defect ('came too late') rather than a substantive outcome ('loses' / 'blocks') — the legal mechanism is visible at title level without clicking, unlike every other outlet in the corpus.
Only headline to use 'again,' signalling accumulation — the pattern of repeated executive failure is conveyed in the title itself, the highest temporal information density at RSS level.
Only outlet to run a birthright citizenship headline alongside the hush money headline, making it the sole outlet whose homepage exposes all three simultaneous judicial fronts of August 28.

Sole outlet contributing a stale 2017 headline ('Federal judge in Hawaii extends order blocking Trump's travel ban') — entirely unrelated to the 2026 hush money proceedings, leaving China absent from the headline story.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, eight of ten live outlets reduce three simultaneous judicial rulings to a single frame — a court blocking Trump's bid to move his hush money conviction — with defeat verbs ('loses,' 'rejects,' 'blocks') dominating every title; the pro-Palestinian deportation and birthright citizenship rulings are invisible to most RSS readers, and Reason alone exposes the procedural rationale rather than the bare outcome.
